does: Cooks a flattened bird or flat pieces of meat skin side down on a hot pan or grill with a heavy weight on top, so that the whole skin stays pressed to the heat and turns evenly crisp.

intro.what: The weight keeps every part of the skin pressed against the hot metal.
intro.why: Even contact gives an even, crisp skin and quick cooking, which a bird left loose on a grill never gets.

how: Flatten the food first so it lies level.
Heat a heavy frying pan, ridged pan or grill to a steady medium heat.
Lay the food skin side down and set a second heavy pan on top, weighed down with tins or a stone.
Leave it alone until the skin is deep gold and crisp, then lift the weight, turn the food and finish it, often in the oven.

cues.text: A steady, even sizzle, not a fierce spit.
The skin is an even deep gold all over, with no pale patches.

mistakes.mistake: Too high a heat, so the skin burns before the meat below has cooked.
mistakes.fix: Use a medium heat and finish the meat in the oven.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the weight often to look, so the skin loses contact and colours in patches.
mistakes.fix: Leave it in place until the skin has crisped.

quiz.question: What does the weight on top do?
choices: It keeps the whole skin pressed to the heat so it crisps evenly.
It squeezes the juices out on purpose.
It stops the pan from smoking.
quiz.because: The point is even contact between skin and hot metal.

quiz.question: Which side goes down first?
quiz.because: The skin side goes down under the weight, so that it crisps.

quiz.question: What should you see before you turn the food?
choices: Pale skin with a few dark spots.
An even deep gold, crisp skin.
quiz.because: Turn only when the whole skin is an even deep gold.

quiz.question: The skin was black before the meat was done. What would you change?
choices: Use a medium heat and finish the meat in the oven.
quiz.because: Moderate heat lets the skin colour while the oven finishes the meat.

comes_after.why: A bird must lie flat before a weight can press all of its skin to the heat.

variant_of.differs: The food lies flat on a hot pan or grill with a weight on top, so all the skin stays pressed to the heat, where a plain grill leaves the food loose on the bars.
